item.title: Reconsider a Review That Calls a Play Nostalgic
item.audience: readers of a local theatre review
item.prompt_text: A review says a play idealises an old neighbourhood because its characters often remember a closed laundrette. In the play, a former customer recalls long conversations while waiting for the washing. A former attendant remembers hours of unpaid closing work. In the last scene, the two use the laundrette keys to open a box of letters and choose which letters can be read aloud. Write a critical response that engages fairly with the review and uses the scene details to offer a different interpretation.
item.target_grammar: Concession, qualification, parallel contrasts, and precise interpretation of dramatic action.
item.target_structure: Represent the review fairly, compare the two memories, analyse the final action, and state a qualified interpretation.

checklist.point: Treat the reviewer’s reason for reading the play as nostalgic fairly.
Explain what changes when the attendant's memory is considered.
Analyse the box of letters and the decision to read selectively.
Give a defensible alternative interpretation rather than an absolute claim.
